questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If cot θ = 12/5 and θ is an acute angle, find the value of (csc θ - sin θ).
questions.solution:
cot θ = 12/5 implies Adjacent = 12, Opposite = 5.
By Pythagorean triplet (5, 12, 13), Hypotenuse = 13.
csc θ = 13/5 and sin θ = 5/13.
csc θ - sin θ = 13/5 - 5/13 = (169 - 25) / 65 = 144/65.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet: Triplet (5, 12, 13). csc θ - sin θ = cos²θ / sin θ = (12/13)² / (5/13) = 144 / 65.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The side of a square is increased by 5 cm, as a result of which its area increases by 155 cm². Find the original length of the side of the square.
questions.solution:
Let original side be s.
(s + 5)² - s² = 155.
s² + 10s + 25 - s² = 155.
10s = 130 ⇒ s = 13 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Delta Rule: Area increase = 2sx + x². Here x = 5: 10s + 25 = 155 ⇒ 10s = 130 ⇒ s = 13 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.topic: Circle - Parallel Chords on Opposite Sides
questions.question: In a circle of radius 29 cm, two parallel chords of length 40 cm and 42 cm are drawn on opposite sides of the centre. Find the perpendicular distance between the two chords.
questions.solution:
Perpendicular from centre bisects chords:
Half-chord 1 = 40/2 = 20 cm. Distance d₁ = √(29² - 20²) = 21 cm.
Half-chord 2 = 42/2 = 21 cm. Distance d₂ = √(29² - 21²) = 20 cm.
Since chords are on opposite sides of the centre, total distance = d₁ + d₂ = 21 + 20 = 41 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet (20, 21, 29): The two distances are simply the counterpart legs: 21 cm and 20 cm. Sum = 21 + 20 = 41 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Two ships are sailing in the sea on opposite sides of a 120 m high lighthouse. The angles of elevation of the top of the lighthouse from the two ships are 30° and 45° respectively. Find the distance between the two ships.
questions.solution:
Let lighthouse be h = 120 m.
Distance to ship 1 = h cot 30° = 120√3 m.
Distance to ship 2 = h cot 45° = 120(1) = 120 m.
Since they are on opposite sides, total distance = 120√3 + 120 = 120(√3 + 1) m.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Formula: Opposite sides: d = h(cot θ₁ + cot θ₂) = 120(√3 + 1) m.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A right pyramid has a square base of side 12 cm. If its vertical height is 15 cm, find the volume of the pyramid.
questions.solution:
Volume = (1/3) × Base Area × height.
Base Area = 12 × 12 = 144 cm².
Volume = (1/3) × 144 × 15 = 144 × 5 = 720 cm³.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If x ∈ {3, 6, 9} and y ∈ {2, 4, 8}, find the maximum possible value of the expression (x² - 2y) / y.
questions.solution:
(x² - 2y) / y = (x² / y) - 2.
To maximise, choose largest x = 9 (x² = 81) and smallest y = 2.
Max value = 81/2 - 2 = 40.5 - 2 = 38.5.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Extrema Trick: (x²/y) - 2. Max x = 9, min y = 2 ⇒ 81/2 - 2 = 38.5.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If matrix A = [[3x, 6], [8, x]] is a singular matrix, what is the positive value of x?
questions.solution:
A matrix is singular when its determinant |A| = 0.
|A| = (3x × x) - (6 × 8) = 3x² - 48.
3x² - 48 = 0 ⇒ 3x² = 48 ⇒ x² = 16 ⇒ x = 4.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Determinant: ad - bc = 0 ⇒ 3x² - 48 = 0 ⇒ x² = 16 ⇒ x = 4.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If matrix A = [[5, -2], [3, 4]] and matrix B = [[1, 7], [-1, 2]], find the trace (sum of main diagonal elements) of matrix (2A - 3B).
questions.solution:
Trace(2A - 3B) = 2 Trace(A) - 3 Trace(B).
Trace(A) = 5 + 4 = 9.
Trace(B) = 1 + 2 = 3.
Trace(2A - 3B) = 2(9) - 3(3) = 18 - 9 = 9.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Trace Linearity: Trace(2A - 3B) = 2(9) - 3(3) = 18 - 9 = 9.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Evaluate: 1 / (√7 - √6) - 1 / (√6 - √5) + 1 / (√5 - 2).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Telescoping: Middle roots cancel out: First root + Last constant = √7 + 2.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: In triangle ABC, line segment XY is parallel to BC with X on AB and Y on AC. If Area(ΔAXY) : Area(Trapezoid XBCY) = 4 : 21, find the ratio AX : XB.
questions.solution:
Area(ΔABC) = Area(ΔAXY) + Area(Trapezoid) = 4 + 21 = 25.
Area(ΔAXY) / Area(ΔABC) = 4 / 25.
Since XY || BC, ΔAXY ~ ΔABC.
(AX / AB)² = 4 / 25 ⇒ AX / AB = 2 / 5.
AX = 2 units, AB = 5 units ⇒ XB = 5 - 2 = 3 units.
Ratio AX : XB = 2 : 3.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Ratio Trick: Total area = 25, top area = 4. Side ratio AX : AB = √4 : √25 = 2 : 5. Then AX : XB = 2 : (5 - 2) = 2 : 3.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: From an external point P, tangent PT of length 15 cm is drawn to a circle. A secant line through P cuts the circle at points A and B. If PA = 9 cm, what is the length of chord AB?
questions.solution:
By Secant-Tangent Theorem: PT² = PA × PB.
15² = 9 × PB ⇒ 225 = 9 × PB ⇒ PB = 25 cm.
Chord AB = PB - PA = 25 - 9 = 16 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Formula: PB = PT²/PA = 225/9 = 25. Chord AB = 25 - 9 = 16 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A grocer professes to sell sugar at a loss of 10% on the cost price, but uses a false weight of 800 g instead of 1 kg. Find his actual overall profit or loss percentage.
questions.solution:
Let cost price of 1000 g be ₹1000.
Customer pays for 1 kg with 10% discount = ₹900.
Actual cost incurred by grocer for 800 g = ₹800.
Profit = 900 - 800 = ₹100.
Profit % = (100 / 800) × 100 = 12.5% profit.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Multiplier: Overall Multiplier = (90/100) × (1000/800) = 0.9 × 1.25 = 1.125 ⇒ 12.5% profit.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A is 40% more efficient than B. If B alone can complete a piece of work in 28 days, in how many days can A and B working together finish the same work?
questions.solution:
Efficiency ratio: A : B = 140 : 100 = 7 : 5.
Total work = Efficiency of B × Days = 5 × 28 = 140 units.
Combined efficiency of (A + B) = 7 + 5 = 12 units/day.
Time taken = 140 / 12 = 35 / 3 = 11 2/3 days.

questions.question: The difference between compound interest (compounded annually) and simple interest on a certain principal sum for 3 years at 10% per annum is ₹620. Find the principal sum.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If the 7-digit number 89x642y is divisible by 72, find the value of (3x - 2y) for the largest single-digit value of y.
questions.solution:
72 = 8 × 9.
Divisibility by 8: last 3 digits '42y' must be div by 8. 424 / 8 = 53 ⇒ y = 4 (only digit).
For y = 4, number is 89x6424.
Divisibility by 9: sum of digits 8+9+x+6+4+2+4 = 33 + x must be multiple of 9 ⇒ 33 + x = 36 ⇒ x = 3.
Value of 3x - 2y = 3(3) - 2(4) = 9 - 8 = 1.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Divisibility: Last 3 digits 424 is div by 8 ⇒ y = 4. Sum = 33 + x = 36 ⇒ x = 3. 3(3) - 2(4) = 1.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The speed of a boat in still water is 15 km/h and the speed of the river current is 3 km/h. The boat travels 36 km downstream and returns immediately to the starting point. Find the total time taken for the round trip.
questions.solution:
Downstream speed = 15 + 3 = 18 km/h.
Upstream speed = 15 - 3 = 12 km/h.
Time downstream = 36 / 18 = 2 hours.
Time upstream = 36 / 12 = 3 hours.
Total time = 2 + 3 = 5 hours.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Quick Sum: 36/18 + 36/12 = 2 + 3 = 5 hours.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Find the volume of a regular tetrahedron whose edge length is 6 cm.
questions.solution:
A regular tetrahedron has 4 equilateral triangle faces.
Volume = (√2 / 12) × a³.
For a = 6: Volume = (√2 / 12) × 6³ = (√2 / 12) × 216 = 18√2 cm³.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Tetrahedron Formula: V = a³√2 / 12 = 216√2 / 12 = 18√2 cm³.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If x - 1/x = 5, find the value of (x³ - 1/x³).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Cube Rule: k³ + 3k = 125 + 15 = 140.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The sides of a right-angled triangle are 15 cm, 20 cm, and 25 cm. Find the inradius (r) of the triangle.
questions.solution:
Inradius of right triangle: r = (a + b - c) / 2.
r = (15 + 20 - 25) / 2 = 10 / 2 = 5 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet Scale: 3-4-5 scaled by 5. Inradius of 3-4-5 is 1. Scaled by 5 ⇒ 1 × 5 = 5 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The length of a rectangular plot is increased by 20% while its breadth is decreased by 10%. Find the percentage change in the area of the plot.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Successive Formula: +20 - 10 - 2 = +8% increase.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Find the square root of (14 + 6√5).
questions.solution:
14 + 6√5 = 14 + 2(3)√5 = 14 + 2√45.
We need two numbers whose product is 45 and sum is 14. The numbers are 9 and 5.
Square root = √9 + √5 = 3 + √5.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Nested Surd: 2ab = 6√5 ⇒ ab = 3√5 ⇒ a=3, b=√5. a² + b² = 9 + 5 = 14. Root = 3 + √5.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: In an examination, 70% of candidates passed in English and 80% passed in Mathematics, while 10% failed in both subjects. If 144 candidates passed in both subjects, find the total number of candidates.
questions.solution:
Failed in English = 30%. Failed in Math = 20%. Failed in both = 10%.
Failed in at least one = 30 + 20 - 10 = 40%.
Passed in both subjects = 100% - 40% = 60%.
60% of Total = 144 ⇒ Total = (144 × 100) / 60 = 240.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A chord of length 48 cm is at a perpendicular distance of 10 cm from the centre of a circle. What is the radius of the circle?
questions.solution:
Perpendicular from centre bisects chord: half-chord = 48/2 = 24 cm.
Radius r = √(24² + 10²) = √(576 + 100) = √676 = 26 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet (10, 24, 26): Standard scaled triplet (5, 12, 13) × 2 = (10, 24, 26). Radius = 26 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Find the total surface area of a regular pyramid whose base is an equilateral triangle of side 6 cm and whose slant height is 10 cm.
questions.solution:
Base Area = (√3/4) × 6² = 9√3 cm².
Lateral Surface Area = (1/2) × Base Perimeter × slant height = (1/2) × 18 × 10 = 90 cm².
Total Surface Area = 90 + 9√3 cm².
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Surface Formula: LSA = (1/2)(18)(10) = 90. Base = 9√3. TSA = 90 + 9√3 cm².

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The base of a right prism is an equilateral triangle of side 8 cm. If the vertical height of the prism is 12 cm, find its volume.
questions.solution:
Volume of prism = Base Area × height.
Base Area = (√3/4) × 8² = 16√3 cm².
Volume = 16√3 × 12 = 192√3 cm³.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Prism Rule: V = A_base × h = (16√3)(12) = 192√3 cm³.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If u ∈ {2, 5, 8} and v ∈ {1, 3, 9}, find the minimum possible value of (u² + v²) / (uv).
questions.solution:
(u² + v²)/(uv) = (u/v) + (v/u). The minimum of t + 1/t is 2 (when t = 1).
We want u/v as close to 1 as possible.
Best pair is u = 2, v = 3 (or u = 8, v = 9):
For u = 8, v = 9: (64 + 81)/72 = 145/72 ≈ 2.014.
Wait! u = 8, v = 9 gives 145 / 72 = 2.014! Let's check: 8/9 = 0.888... and 9/8 = 1.125. Sum = 2.014.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Extrema Trick: u=8, v=9 are closest! (64 + 81) / 72 = 145/72 ≈ 2.01.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A circle has a radius of 61 cm. A chord is drawn at a perpendicular distance of 11 cm from the centre. What is the total length of the chord?
questions.solution:
Half-chord = √(61² - 11²) = √(3721 - 121) = √3600 = 60 cm.
Total chord length = 2 × 60 = 120 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet (11, 60, 61): Half chord is 60 cm. Total length = 2 × 60 = 120 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A chord of length 70 cm is drawn inside a circle of radius 37 cm. What is the perpendicular distance of the chord from the centre of the circle?
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Triplet (12, 35, 37): r = 37, half-chord = 35 ⇒ distance = 12 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: From the top of a 60 m high cliff, the angle of depression of a boat changes from 60° to 45° as it sails directly away from the cliff. Find the distance sailed by the boat during this time.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If sec θ = 41/40 and θ is an acute angle, find the value of (1 - sin θ) / (1 + sin θ).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Half-Angle Identity: (1 - sin θ)/(1 + sin θ) = ((1 - sin θ)/cos θ)² = (sec θ - tan θ)² = (41/40 - 9/40)² = (32/40)² = (4/5)² = 16/25.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: The perimeter of a square is increased by 16 cm, as a result of which its area increases by 120 cm². Find the original perimeter of the square.
questions.solution:
Perimeter increases by 16 cm ⇒ Side increases by 16/4 = 4 cm.
(s + 4)² - s² = 120 ⇒ 8s + 16 = 120 ⇒ 8s = 104 ⇒ s = 13 cm.
Original perimeter = 4s = 4 × 13 = 52 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Perimeter Delta: Δs = 4. 8s + 16 = 120 ⇒ s = 13. Perimeter = 4 × 13 = 52 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: In triangle ABC, medians AD and BE intersect at centroid G. If the area of triangle ABC is 72 cm², what is the area of triangle AGE?
questions.solution:
The three medians of a triangle divide it into 6 triangles of equal area.
Area of ΔAGE = Area(ΔABC) / 6 = 72 / 6 = 12 cm².
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Centroid Rule: All 6 median-split triangles have equal area: 72/6 = 12 cm².

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: From an external point P, two secants PAB and PCD are drawn to a circle. If PA = 4 cm, AB = 5 cm, and PC = 3 cm, find the length of chord CD.
questions.solution:
By Secant Power Theorem: PA × PB = PC × PD.
PB = PA + AB = 4 + 5 = 9 cm.
4 × 9 = 3 × PD ⇒ 36 = 3 × PD ⇒ PD = 12 cm.
Chord CD = PD - PC = 12 - 3 = 9 cm.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Secant Rule: PD = 36/3 = 12. Chord CD = 12 - 3 = 9 cm.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: Pipe A can fill a tank in 12 min and Pipe B in 15 min. A waste pipe C empties water at the rate of 3 gallons per minute. When all three pipes are opened together, the tank is filled in 10 min. Find the capacity of the tank.
questions.solution:
Rate of C = (1/12 + 1/15) - 1/10 = (5 + 4 - 6)/60 = 3/60 = 1/20 per minute.
Pipe C can empty the full tank in 20 minutes.
Capacity = 20 min × 3 gallons/min = 60 gallons.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Net Rate: C's rate = 9/60 - 6/60 = 3/60 = 1/20. Time = 20 min. Capacity = 20 × 3 = 60 gallons.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: An article with a marked price of ₹1,500 is sold for ₹1,104 after two successive discounts. If the first discount is 8%, find the rate of the second discount.
questions.solution:
Price after 8% discount = 1500 × (1 - 0.08) = ₹1380.
Remaining discount = 1380 - 1104 = ₹276.
Second discount % = (276 / 1380) × 100 = 20%.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If the compound interest on a sum for 2 years at 15% per annum is ₹3,225, find the simple interest on the same sum at the same rate for 2 years.
questions.solution:
Effective 2-year CI rate = 15 + 15 + (15 × 15)/100 = 32.25%.
Effective 2-year SI rate = 15 × 2 = 30%.
32.25% corresponds to ₹3225 ⇒ 1% = ₹100.
Simple Interest = 30% = 30 × 100 = ₹3,000.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Effective Rate: 32.25% = ₹3225 ⇒ 30% = ₹3,000 directly.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If the 6-digit number 43x82y is divisible by 99, find the value of (x + y).
questions.solution:
99 = 9 × 11.
Divisibility by 9: Sum of digits = 4 + 3 + x + 8 + 2 + y = 17 + x + y.
17 + x + y must be a multiple of 9 (either 18 or 27).
Divisibility by 11: (4 + x + 2) - (3 + 8 + y) = (x + 6) - (y + 11) = x - y - 5.
For integer digits, x - y - 5 = -11 ⇒ y - x = 6.
With y - x = 6 and x + y = 10: 2y = 16 ⇒ y = 8, x = 2.
Both are valid single digits! Value of x + y = 10.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Divisibility: Sum of digits 17 + (x+y) must be 27 ⇒ x + y = 10.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A train travels 120 km at 60 km/h, the next 180 km at 90 km/h, and the last 100 km at 50 km/h. Find the average speed of the train for the entire journey.
questions.solution:
Time 1 = 120/60 = 2 hours.
Time 2 = 180/90 = 2 hours.
Time 3 = 100/50 = 2 hours.
Total distance = 120 + 180 + 100 = 400 km.
Total time = 2 + 2 + 2 = 6 hours.
Average Speed = 400 / 6 = 66.67 km/h.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Total Time: Total Distance / Total Time = 400 / 6 = 66.67 km/h.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.topic: Right Triangle Area from Inradius & Circumradius
questions.question: The inradius and circumradius of a right-angled triangle are 3 cm and 12.5 cm respectively. Find the area of the triangle.
questions.solution:
Hypotenuse c = 2R = 2 × 12.5 = 25 cm.
Inradius r = (a + b - c)/2 ⇒ 3 = (a + b - 25)/2 ⇒ a + b = 31 cm.
Semi-perimeter s = (a + b + c)/2 = (31 + 25)/2 = 28 cm.
Area = r × s = 3 × 28 = 84 cm².
(Sides are 7, 24, 25; Area = 1/2 × 7 × 24 = 84 cm²).
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Formula: Area = r(2R + r) = 3(25 + 3) = 3(28) = 84 cm²!

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: If tan θ + cot θ = 2, find the value of (tan⁷ θ + cot⁷ θ).
questions.solution:
tan θ + 1/tan θ = 2 implies tan θ = 1 (θ = 45°).
cot θ = 1.
tan⁷(45°) + cot⁷(45°) = 1⁷ + 1⁷ = 1 + 1 = 2.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Standard Value: Whenever tan θ + cot θ = 2, tan θ = cot θ = 1. Value is always 2.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A boat takes twice as long to row upstream as to row downstream for the same distance. If the speed of the current is 4 km/h, find the speed of the boat in still water.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A container contains 80 litres of pure milk. 8 litres of milk is drawn out and replaced with water. This operation is performed one more time. How much pure milk is left in the container?
questions.solution:
Remaining liquid = Initial × [1 - (x / V)]ⁿ.
Remaining = 80 × [1 - (8 / 80)]² = 80 × (9/10)² = 80 × (81/100) = 64.8 litres.

questions.subject: Quantitative Aptitude
questions.question: A and B enter into a partnership. A invests ₹20,000 for 9 months and B invests ₹30,000 for 6 months. If the total annual profit is ₹36,000, find A's share of the profit.
questions.shortcut: ⚡ 5-Sec Ratio: 180k : 180k = 1 : 1. Equal split = ₹18,000.
